problem_text:
A municipality aims to devise a comprehensive waste‑water purification strategy to lower the total biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) discharge from a set of industrial effluent outlets. Initially, no treatment technologies have been implemented.

The characteristics of each discharge outlet are as follows:
* For Outlet 1, the BOD coefficient is 2.356, and the flow rate is 138.399.
* For Outlet 2, the BOD coefficient is 2.588, and the flow rate is 292.403.
* For Outlet 3, the BOD coefficient is 1.248, and the flow rate is 120.115.
* For Outlet 4, the BOD coefficient is 2.312, and the flow rate is 57.793.
* For Outlet 5, the BOD coefficient is 1.289, and the flow rate is 295.905.
* For Outlet 6, the BOD coefficient is 1.84, and the flow rate is 206.628.
* For Outlet 7, the BOD coefficient is 1.021, and the flow rate is 260.601.
* For Outlet 8, the BOD coefficient is 2.214, and the flow rate is 192.745.
* For Outlet 9, the BOD coefficient is 2.499, and the flow rate is 147.392.
* For Outlet 10, the BOD coefficient is 2.72, and the flow rate is 198.798.

To curtail the BOD load, several purification technologies are accessible, each distinguished by a specific removal rate:
* Technology1 reduces the pollutant by 21%
* Technology2 reduces the pollutant by 30%
* Technology3 reduces the pollutant by 34%
* Technology4 reduces the pollutant by 65%
* Technology5 reduces the pollutant by 88%
* Technology6 reduces the pollutant by 57%
* Technology7 reduces the pollutant by 50%
* Technology8 reduces the pollutant by 71%
* Technology9 reduces the pollutant by 54%
* Technology10 reduces the pollutant by 14%

Deploying a technology at an outlet entails an additional expenditure per unit of flow. The cost matrix for every outlet–technology pairing is provided below:

| Outlet \ Technology | Tech1 | Tech2 | Tech3 | Tech4 | Tech5 | Tech6 | Tech7 | Tech8 | Tech9 | Tech10 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Outlet 1 | 51.067 | 67.44 | 31.324 | 159.139 | 157.78 | 183.537 | 94.317 | 14.738 | 101.706 | 105.01 |
| Outlet 2 | 46.14 | 185.491 | 149.164 | 109.489 | 157.351 | 37.226 | 175.642 | 166.206 | 188.225 | 138.576 |
| Outlet 3 | 35.216 | 147.668 | 97.28 | 145.599 | 109.246 | 10.781 | 187.144 | 140.54 | 122.915 | 26.544 |
| Outlet 4 | 98.706 | 18.767 | 108.91 | 135.207 | 69.371 | 119.736 | 69.307 | 179.506 | 70.967 | 46.584 |
| Outlet 5 | 62.563 | 70.638 | 93.812 | 32.354 | 38.371 | 61.991 | 12.899 | 128.36 | 107.672 | 49.25 |
| Outlet 6 | 76.56 | 70.512 | 36.896 | 143.827 | 63.821 | 56.517 | 23.536 | 126.52 | 74.36 | 94.293 |
| Outlet 7 | 34.714 | 99.44 | 138.344 | 30.126 | 20.222 | 91.028 | 44.007 | 123.263 | 122.624 | 168.873 |
| Outlet 8 | 142.879 | 127.1 | 69.364 | 165.314 | 145.451 | 137.465 | 111.362 | 195.0 | 153.591 | 98.482 |
| Outlet 9 | 35.041 | 164.442 | 184.741 | 98.972 | 96.561 | 140.051 | 144.941 | 98.425 | 54.022 | 52.521 |
| Outlet 10 | 173.608 | 127.219 | 183.444 | 84.495 | 142.927 | 136.384 | 159.868 | 177.657 | 96.124 | 15.75 |

The municipality must decide how to assign purification technologies to each outlet (outlets may employ several technologies concurrently), and an outlet may also remain partially untreated if needed.
The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate BOD discharge is lowered by at least a fraction P = 0.438 of the baseline load, while minimizing the overall expenditure.
